blocks.content: Both define variables usable inside a Dockerfile, but their lifetimes are completely different: ARG only exists during the build, ENV persists into the running container too.

ARG values are scoped strictly to the build process, useful for things like a version number that only matters while assembling the image. ENV values are baked into the image permanently, visible both during the rest of the build and to the application once it is actually running.

blocks.alt: ARG disappears after the build, ENV does not

blocks.content: 2. What a Running Container Can Actually See
blocks.text: 2. What a Running Container Can Actually See

blocks.content: This is the practical consequence that matters most: an application inside a running container can read any ENV variable that was set, but has no way to see an ARG value at all, it was never carried into the final image.

blocks.alt: Only ENV values are visible once the container is running

3. Bridging the Two When You Need To
blocks.text: 3. Bridging the Two When You Need To

blocks.content: If a build-time value genuinely needs to be visible at runtime too, the common pattern assigns an ARG's value into an ENV variable, which then carries it forward into the running container, giving you the best of both: build-time overridability and runtime visibility.

blocks.alt: Assign an ARG into an ENV to carry it into runtime

blocks.content:
ARG VERSION=1.0
ENV APP_VERSION=$VERSION
# APP_VERSION is now visible inside the running container too

ENV APP_VERSION=$VERSION
# APP_VERSION is now visible inside the running container too

blocks.title: Key Takeaway
points: ARG is build-time only and disappears afterward, ENV persists into the running container and is visible to the actual application.
To make a build-time value visible at runtime, assign the ARG into an ENV variable explicitly.
